subject: series
synopsis: A crime thriller about a lottery winner whose sudden windfall draws dangerous attention from criminals and corrupt figures. Set in a gritty contemporary milieu where unexpected wealth becomes a curse rather than a blessing.

subject: series
synopsis: Jim Butcher's original comics prequel to Storm Front: wizard detective Harry Dresden investigates a savage killing at the Lincoln Park Zoo.

subject: series
synopsis: An adaptation of Joe Hill's novella Rain, in which mysterious nails rain from the sky across America, instantly killing anyone they strike, as survivors try to piece together what happened.
author: Joe Hill

subject: series
synopsis: Robert Kirkman's miniseries following the newly de-powered Jubilee navigating life as a regular teenager without her mutant abilities, exploring identity and belonging beyond the X-Men.
author: Robert Kirkman

subject: series
synopsis: A twelve-issue prestige format limited series by Jim Krueger and Alex Ross in which the Legion of Doom strikes simultaneously at the world, forcing the Justice League to reassemble. Ross's painted art gives it the scope of a mythological epic.

subject: series
synopsis: A six-issue crossover limited series between DC's Justice League and the Saban Mighty Morphin Power Rangers, written by Tom Taylor with art by Stephen Byrne. A fun genre mashup that takes both properties seriously.
author: Tom Taylor

subject: series
synopsis: Zander Cannon's Kaijumax: a maximum-security prison for giant monsters, a darkly comic crime drama in candy-colored tokusatsu style.
author: Zander Cannon

subject: series
synopsis: Toshiki Inoue's manga adaptation of the groundbreaking 2000 Kamen Rider series that revived the franchise — following Godai Yuusuke's battles with the mysterious Grongi creatures.
author: Shotaro Ishinomori

subject: series
synopsis: A Europe Comics series exploring spiritual themes and urban mythology with philosophical depth.

subject: series
synopsis: Sumito Owara's vibrant manga about three high school girls — a concept artist, a producer, and a mechanic — founding an animation club and making anime through sheer creative force. An exhilarating celebration of the artistic process and collaborative ambition.
author: Sumito Owara

subject: series
synopsis: A miniseries by Bruce Jones offering an origin and character study of Wilson Fisk, tracing the Kingpin's rise from poverty to criminal empire with a gritty crime-fiction sensibility.
author: Bruce Jones

subject: series
synopsis: A pivotal limited series set in Japan that fundamentally transformed Kitty Pryde from teenage sidekick into a capable hero, while deepening Wolverine's ties to Japanese culture and honor.
author: Chris Claremont

subject: series
synopsis: A special issue set in the Kong of Skull Island universe, exploring the mythological and tribal origins of the great ape.

subject: series
synopsis: Sammy Harkham's prestigious alternative comics anthology gathering work from the world's most ambitious cartoonists — an essential record of where literary comics were at the turn of the millennium.
author: Sammy Harkham

subject: series
synopsis: A six-issue limited series by Paul Levitz with art by Chris Batista presenting a new retelling of the Legion of Super-Heroes' founding, exploring how the three original Legionnaires came together and the political circumstances that shaped the team.
author: Paul Levitz

subject: series
synopsis: A 2023 Life is Strange miniseries introducing new characters in the Life is Strange universe. Explores themes of memory, identity, and the cost of supernatural powers.

subject: series
synopsis: Dark Horse's archival collections of John Stanley's beloved Little Lulu comics — classic all-ages humor featuring the spirited young heroine and her friends in clever, repeatedly surprising gag strips.
author: John Stanley

subject: series
synopsis: Daniel Clowes's 1986 Fantagraphics series: Lloyd Llewellyn, a hapless 1950s-styled private eye, in retro pop-noir pastiche, Clowes's earliest major work.

subject: series
synopsis: Ann Nocenti and Arthur Adams' seminal miniseries introducing the dimension-hopping rebel Longshot, a slave from an alien media empire who escapes to Earth and becomes entangled with the X-Men.
author: Ann Nocenti

subject: series
synopsis: Tom King and Elsa Charretier's formally inventive Image Comics series about Joan Peterson, a protagonist of vintage romance comics who begins to become aware of her cyclical imprisonment inside genre conventions. A postmodern deconstruction with genuine emotional resonance.
author: Tom King

subject: series
synopsis: Jamie S. Rich and Megan Levens's reimagining of the Frankenstein mythology from the perspective of a scientist obsessed with resurrecting his lost love, set in 1930s America with Art Deco aesthetics and old Hollywood atmosphere.
author: Jamie S. Rich

subject: series
synopsis: Peter David's acclaimed noir-inflected story of Jamie Madrox the Multiple Man running a detective agency, the foundation of the acclaimed X-Factor Investigations run.
author: Peter David

subject: series
synopsis: Rob Liefeld's return to the X-Men sandbox introducing Major X, a mysterious time-traveler from a dark future, in a story heavy on '90s X-Force nostalgia and Liefeld's signature aesthetic.
author: Rob Liefeld

subject: series
synopsis: Pat Mills and Kevin O'Neill's vicious satire follows a law enforcement officer in a near-future San Francisco who hunts and kills superheroes; one of the most savage and intelligent deconstructions of the superhero genre ever published.
author: Pat Mills

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Millar and Tommy Lee Edwards's 2008 1985: a lonely boy in small-town America watches Marvel's villains break into the real world.
author: Mark Millar

subject: series
synopsis: A Marvel horror anthology title from the bronze age featuring supernatural antiheroes including Tigra and Modred the Mystic, part of Marvel's 1970s expansion into horror and monster comics.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Matt Kindt and Marco Rudy's 2013 Marvel Knights: Spider-Man: a drugged Peter Parker fights through 99 villains in a surreal, psychedelic gauntlet.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's prestige reprint series collecting the earliest Timely/Marvel Comics publications — the debut issues of Captain America, Human Torch, Sub-Mariner, and others — in archival hardcover format. Essential for Golden Age scholarship.

subject: series
synopsis: Archival reprints collecting Sub-Mariner's classic Bronze Age series, preserving the adventures of Prince Namor as a complicated anti-hero navigating the surface world and the ocean kingdoms.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Jonathan Maberry's prequel to the Marvel Universe vs. The Punisher story, showing Wolverine's perspective on the viral outbreak that turned Marvel's heroes into cannibalistic predators. Effective horror-survival storytelling within the high-concept premise.
author: Jonathan Maberry

subject: series
synopsis: Rhianna Pratchett and Matthew Dow Smith's 2008 prequel to the Mirror's Edge game: Faith's early days as a runner in a surveillance-state city.

subject: series
synopsis: Fantasy adventure series from MadCave drawing on the universal hero's journey structure, following a protagonist through archetypal trials and transformation.
author: Siike Donnelly, David Hazan

subject: series
synopsis: Crime drama series from MadCave featuring character portraits and stories drawn from the criminal underworld.
author: Jordan Thomas

subject: series
synopsis: Yuki Urushibara's quiet masterpiece follows Ginko, a wandering 'Mushi-shi' who studies and deals with primitive lifeforms called Mushi that inhabit the margins of the natural world. Each self-contained chapter is a contemplative short story exploring humanity's relationship with nature, memory, and the unseen.
author: Yuki Urushibara

subject: series
synopsis: Yoko Akiyama's spinoff manga sends U.A. students on collaborative missions with Pro Heroes, delivering light character-driven team-up stories aimed at fans of the main series.
author: Yoko Akiyama

subject: series
synopsis: Hayao Miyazaki's magnum opus manga, an epic ecological sci-fi fantasy set millennia after an apocalypse, following the princess of a small kingdom navigating warring nations and a toxic jungle; visually stunning, philosophically profound, and one of the greatest manga ever created.
author: Hayao Miyazaki

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's trade paperback reprint line collecting the classic Chris Claremont and Bob McLeod New Mutants run, preserving the formative stories of the next generation of Xavier's students during the early 1980s.
author: Chris Claremont

subject: series
synopsis: Kurt Busiek's attempt to breathe life into Shadowhawk beyond Rob Liefeld's original creation, following a new character who takes up the armor in a more coherent story than the original series. Busiek's craft elevates the concept.
author: Kurt Busiek

subject: series
synopsis: Grant Morrison's radical reinvention of the X-Men stripped away the costumes and injected the franchise with literary ambition, body horror, and genuinely new ideas about mutation and posthumanity.
author: Grant Morrison

subject: series
synopsis: A paranoid espionage thriller in which Nick Fury uncovers a HYDRA conspiracy that has infiltrated the highest levels of S.H.I.E.L.D. itself, written with Cold War urgency.
author: Bob Harras

subject: series
synopsis: P. Craig Russell's Eclipse series of lush adaptations — opera, Kipling's Jungle Book tales and fantasy stories — in his elegant art nouveau line.

subject: series
synopsis: Alex de Campi and Carla Speed McNeil's survival thriller follows American students stranded in a fictional Latin American country after a bus crash, with the group fracturing lethally under pressure.
author: Alex de Campi

subject: series
synopsis: A crime anthology series from Dynamite featuring various noir-themed short stories in the hard-boiled tradition, with multiple creators contributing tales of detectives, criminals, and moral corruption.
author: Lukasz Bogacz

subject: series
synopsis: A webcomic series exploring workplace slice-of-life humor.

subject: series
synopsis: An Antarctic Press series with sci-fi themes and space adventure elements.

subject: series
synopsis: Kevin Huizenga's minicomic anthology series showcasing his trademark blend of suburban observation, metaphysical inquiry, and experimental comics storytelling. Each issue ranges from quiet domestic realism to formally ambitious philosophical fables, establishing Huizenga as one of the most intellectually ambitious cartoonists of his generation.
author: Kevin Huizenga

subject: series
synopsis: James Stokoe's wildly inventive fantasy follows a one-eyed orc outlaw with a gift for cracking things apart in a grotesque, impossibly detailed world drawn with Stokoe's trademark obsessive linework and biological excess.
author: James Stokoe

subject: series
synopsis: Kieron Gillen and Adam Kubert's sequel to the original Wolverine Origin, following young James Howlett's feral years in the Canadian wilderness and first encounters with Creed, featuring Gillen's mythic sensibility applied to classic Marvel history.
author: Kieron Gillen

subject: series
synopsis: Phil Jimenez's Vertigo series exploring a young British woman's journey into a dimension parallel to our own where magic is real. Ambitious mythology-building with Jimenez's detailed art style, though the series ended prematurely.
author: Phil Jimenez

subject: series
synopsis: A series featuring Pantha, a Were-panther character from the Vampirella mythology, in solo horror-action adventures separate from her usual supporting role.

subject: series
synopsis: Lucien De Gieter's long-running Belgian comic series following Papyrus, a young fisherman who discovers a magical sword in the Nile and becomes embroiled in the mysteries and dangers of ancient Egypt. A beloved all-ages adventure beloved by generations of European readers.
author: Lucien De Gieter

subject: series
synopsis: The official comic adaptation of Paizo's beloved tabletop RPG, following the iconic Pathfinder Society adventurers through high-fantasy sword-and-sorcery quests. Competent licensed fantasy comics aimed squarely at fans of the game.

subject: series
synopsis: Hidenori Kusaka's manga adaptation of the Pokémon games takes a more dramatic, adventurous approach than the anime — protagonists like Red and Blue face genuine danger, and the story engages more seriously with the implications of the game world. A beloved alternative to the anime for older fans.
author: Hidenori Kusaka

subject: series
synopsis: Victor Santos' stylish spy thriller follows a retired assassin called the Black Kaiser who is pulled back in for one last job in a brutal, graphically inventive story rendered in stark black-and-white with colour-coded key visuals.
author: Victor Santos

subject: series
synopsis: David Walker's revival of the classic Heroes for Hire partnership, balancing nostalgic affection for Luke Cage and Danny Rand's friendship with fresh street-level adventures and strong supporting cast work.
author: David Walker

subject: series
synopsis: Jeff Lemire and Andrea Sorrentino's sci-fi story about the first animals sent into space — Laika and others — and what they encountered. Sorrentino's experimental page design is extraordinary; the emotional resonance around real history is genuine.
author: Jeff Lemire

subject: series
synopsis: Historical thriller series from MadCave set around the real Nazi underground construction project known as Project Riese, blending espionage and wartime intrigue.
author: Zac Thompson

subject: series
synopsis: Garth Ennis's brutal, uncompromising MAX imprint run strips the Punisher of all superhero fantasy and plants him in a hyper-realistic world of organized crime, military corruption, and institutional rot. The definitive adult take on Frank Castle, relentless and morally unsparing.
author: Garth Ennis

subject: series
synopsis: Terry Moore's supernatural horror series following Rachel Beck, who digs herself out of her own grave with no memory of how she died — beginning an investigation into supernatural forces plaguing her small New England town with ties to the Salem witch trials.
author: Terry Moore

subject: series
synopsis: Donny Cates and Lisandro Estherren's horror series following the Bowmans, a vampire family living quietly in rural Texas and running a BBQ joint — until old grudges erupt into a blood feud that threatens to consume everyone around them.
author: Donny Cates

subject: series
synopsis: David Boswell's cult underground comic featuring the magnificently antisocial milkman Reid Fleming, who terrorizes his customers, bosses, and romantic targets with gleeful ineptitude and spectacular rudeness. The strip's deadpan absurdism and perfectly rendered grouchiness earned it a devoted following across its sporadic publication history.
author: David Boswell

subject: series
synopsis: Joe Harris and Megan Hutchison's horror mystery set in the LA rock music scene, following a groupie obsessed with rock legends who discovers a dark conspiracy linking rock stardom to occult sacrifice and demonic deals. Captures genuine period atmosphere of 1970s rock culture.
author: Joe Harris

subject: series
synopsis: Kieron Gillen and Steven Sanders's 2010 S.W.O.R.D.: Abigail Brand and Beast run Earth's alien-defence agency while Henry Gyrich schemes to deport every alien.

subject: series
synopsis: A standalone Sabretooth noir set in 1920s Madripoor exploring Victor Creed's brutal mercenary past before he became a fixture of the X-Men world.
author: Victor LaValle

subject: series
synopsis: A Krakoa-era series following a newly heroic Sabretooth leading a team of mutant outcasts in opposition to Orchis, part of the broader mutant revolution of the era.
author: Victor LaValle

subject: series
synopsis: Greg Pak and Evan Narcisse's 2025 Sam Wilson: Captain America mini-series.

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's comic adaptation of Genndy Tartakovsky's beloved Cartoon Network series faithfully captures the show's cinematic visual language and the samurai's endless quest to find a way back in time to defeat the demon Aku. Writers and artists managed to evoke the series' distinctive style of sparse dialogue, dynamic action, and meditative atmosphere.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Hisae Iwaoka's quiet sci-fi manga follows Mitsu, a 15-year-old who becomes a window cleaner on a ring station orbiting a now-preserved Earth. A gentle, contemplative character study about the longing to touch the world below and the dignity of working-class labor in a stratified space society.
author: Hisae Iwaoka

subject: series
synopsis: A Zenescope comic adaptation drawing on the Seven Deadly Sins concept popularized by the David Fincher film, following investigators confronting a serial killer whose murders are staged around the seven deadly sins. A 7-issue horror/crime miniseries with dark, gritty tone.

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Michael Bendis and Gabriele Dell'Otto's high-stakes espionage thriller reveals Nick Fury's secret unauthorized mission against Latveria, with Dell'Otto's painted art elevating it into one of the era's most visually striking events.
author: Brian Michael Bendis

subject: series
synopsis: Grant Morrison's four-issue limited series reimagining the Frankenstein monster as a pulp adventure hero battling supernatural threats for S.H.A.D.E. Thrillingly inventive and propulsively plotted — the most action-packed entry in the Seven Soldiers project.
author: Grant Morrison

subject: series
synopsis: Grant Morrison's four-issue Mister Miracle series from the Seven Soldiers project, following Scott Free in a deeply surreal, identity-dissolving story that presaged Morrison's later Final Crisis work on the character.
author: Grant Morrison

subject: series
synopsis: Dynamite's revival of the classic jungle heroine Sheena, one of comics' original female leads, in modern adventure stories set in an African jungle fighting poachers and supernatural threats.

subject: series
synopsis: A dark miniseries following the Inhumans after the events of Son of M, as Black Bolt wages war against humanity in response to the depowering of Quicksilver and Luna, with grim political consequences.
author: David Hine

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's comic adaptation of the 2018 film Solo: A Star Wars Story, following a young Han Solo's early adventures including meeting Chewbacca and Lando Calrissian.
author: Robbie Thompson

subject: series
synopsis: Dark fantasy action series from MadCave featuring a supernatural protagonist with the power to take or manipulate souls in a world of occult conflict.
author: Jeannine Acheson, Tom Sniegoski

subject: series
synopsis: Ablaze's adaptation of Leiji Matsumoto's iconic space opera, following the renegade Captain Harlock and his crew aboard the Arcadia as they rebel against a corrupt Earth government; a faithful comics reimagining of the classic anime/manga property.

subject: series
synopsis: Paul Jenkins and Humberto Ramos's 2003 Spectacular Spider-Man: Venom, the Lizard and Aunt May stories in a character-driven 27-issue run.
author: Paul Jenkins

subject: series
synopsis: A Spider-Man limited series tied to the Breakout event, following the web-slinger's response to a mass super-villain prison escape that also spawned the formation of the New Avengers.

subject: series
synopsis: A fun miniseries in which the Kravinoff family hunts a reluctant Alyosha Kravinoff rather than Spider-Man, examining the legacy and burden of the Kraven the Hunter name.
author: Ron Zimmerman

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2019 Spider-Verse mini-series: the mysterious Spider-Zero hops between alternate spider-heroes' worlds, each issue a variant showcase.

subject: series
synopsis: John Ostrander and Jan Duursema's acclaimed Dark Horse series set 130 years after the films, following Cade Skywalker - a descendant of the Skywalker line turned bounty hunter - in a galaxy conquered by a new Sith Empire, celebrated for its bold world-building and complex characters.
author: John Ostrander

subject: series
synopsis: Image's 2023 anthology of zodiac-themed stories by creators including Saladin Ahmed, Mirka Andolfo and James Tynion IV.

subject: series
synopsis: Comics based on Cartoon Network's beloved animated series following Steven Universe and the Crystal Gems, continuing the emotional, mythology-rich stories of the show.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Jai Nitz and Brian Buccellato's DC anthology collecting backup Suicide Squad stories exploring less-seen members of Task Force X. A companion volume to the main series for completists.
author: Jai Nitz

subject: series
synopsis: A Lion Forge Catalyst Prime series spotlighting Jonah, a teenager with Down syndrome who gains superpowers after the Catalyst Prime cosmic event, exploring disability, identity, and heroism in an accessible and thoughtful story.

subject: series
synopsis: Brainiac attacks New Krypton as the New Krypton storyline reaches its climax.
author: James Robinson

subject: series
synopsis: A heartfelt limited series by Tom King and Andy Kubert in which Superman pursues an alien who has kidnapped a girl named Alice across the cosmos, told in two-page chapter installments. author: Tom King

subject: series
synopsis: Sara Kenney and John Watkiss's near-future medical thriller set in a world where antibiotics have stopped working, following a surgeon who goes off the books to save patients the system has abandoned. subject: series
synopsis: A manga adaptation of Reki Kawahara's reboot of the original SAO arc, following Kirito and Asuna as they fight floor-by-floor through Aincrad in greater detail than the original telling. A solid companion piece for SAO fans that rewards readers already familiar with the light novel.
author: Reki Kawahara

subject: series
synopsis: Ken Siu-Chong and UDON's 2002 four-issue Taskmaster mini, the mimic mercenary in an anime-styled action story.

subject: series
synopsis: IDW sequel continuing the post-apocalyptic TMNT story following the conclusion of The Last Ronin.

subject: series
synopsis: A six-issue limited series spinning out of Teen Titans, focusing on Clock King assembling a team of teenage villains and running a meta-human fight club. Written by Sean McKeever with art by Joe Bennett, it was a dark tie-in to the Final Crisis era.

subject: series
synopsis: Fuse's spin-off manga following Rimuru's monster nation from the perspectives of its inhabitants, expanding the TenSura world beyond the main character's viewpoint.
author: Fuse

subject: series
synopsis: Another TenSura spin-off focusing on three young women from the Tempest nation in adventures during Rimuru's early reign. Primarily for fans who want more world-building content.
author: Fuse

subject: series
synopsis: Top Cow's spy thriller series following a team of agents navigating corporate espionage and superhuman threats in a world where information is the ultimate weapon. Competent early 2000s action-thriller from the Top Cow stable.

subject: series
synopsis: Jonathan Hickman and Tomm Coker's extraordinarily dense occult thriller positing that global financial capitalism is secretly sustained by a pact with dark forces. Deliberately oblique, intellectually demanding, and visually striking — unfinished but compelling.
author: Jonathan Hickman

subject: series
synopsis: Liam Sharp's painted-quality art drives this atmospheric 6-issue miniseries that sends Batman and Wonder Woman deep into Celtic myth after a Fae murder mystery. author: Liam Sharp

subject: series
synopsis: James O'Barr's The Crow: Eric Draven returns from the grave, guided by a crow, to avenge his and his fiancée's murders — a raw, grief-soaked cult classic.

subject: series
synopsis: Jennie Breeden's autobiographical webcomic chronicling her life as a convention-going geek and artist, mixing diary comic strip humor with affectionate observations about genre fandom culture and daily mishaps.
author: Jennie Breeden

subject: series
synopsis: A supernatural horror series from Dynamite featuring a group of holy warriors and occult investigators confronting a demonic incursion threatening the world. Dark religious horror with action elements.
author: Joshua Hale Fialkov

subject: series
synopsis: A comics continuation of the Fly horror franchise, set years after the original story with a new generation dealing with the horror of the Brundle family legacy.

subject: series
synopsis: Comics based on Disney's beloved Haunted Mansion attraction featuring ghost stories and supernatural adventures.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Action-fantasy series from MadCave following the last surviving members of an ancient order of wardens tasked with protecting the world from supernatural threats.
author: Amit Tishler, Elliot Sperl

subject: series
synopsis: Remastered and recolored collected edition of Sam Kieth's The Maxx — the surreal superhero mystery that remains one of the most psychologically complex comics of the 1990s.
author: Sam Kieth

subject: series
synopsis: Margaret Stohl's run on Captain Marvel during the Secret Empire event, following Carol Danvers leading the Alpha Flight space program as Hydra's America-First government isolates Earth from the universe; a solid Carol Danvers showcase during a turbulent period.
author: Margaret Stohl

subject: series
synopsis: Peter Milligan and Sean Phillips's 1998 Vertigo series: a prim woman discovers she has multiple personalities as a Monkey God prepares to arrive on Earth.

subject: series
synopsis: Dynamite's licensed comic adaptation of the beloved Cartoon Network animated series, following the superhero kindergartners Blossom, Bubbles, and Buttercup defending Townsville.

subject: series
synopsis: Howard Mackie's New 52 series following young metahumans escaping N.O.W.H.E.R.E.'s control in a road-trip superhero format. One of the less successful New 52 concepts that was cancelled after a brief run.
author: Howard Mackie

subject: series
synopsis: A TokyoPop manga about a mysterious tarot reader and supernatural mysteries with beautiful art.
author: Sang-sun Park

subject: series
synopsis: Declan Shalvey's 2024 Dynamite Terminator: a gritty relaunch of the time-travelling killer-robot saga.

subject: series
synopsis: A Marvel crime series exploring organized crime in a superhero universe.

subject: series
synopsis: Bruce Jones's DC series reviving the classic Showcase concept by dropping World War II soldiers onto a prehistoric island filled with dinosaurs. A pulp premise executed with more interest in action than character.
author: Bruce Jones

subject: series
synopsis: Mathieu Mariolle's Thorgal Universe spinoff following Thorgal's son Wolf as he navigates the Norse world in his own coming-of-age adventures.
author: Mathieu Mariolle

subject: series
synopsis: A prequel spin-off series expanding the mythology of Thorgal, the legendary Belgian fantasy-adventure saga by Van Hamme and Rosinski, exploring the backstories of key characters in the Viking-meets-alien-civilization world. Maintains the grand adventure scope of the original while filling in narrative gaps.
author: Yves Sente

subject: series
synopsis: A digital-first vertical Infinity Comic adaptation or companion to Jason Aaron's landmark God Butcher arc, bringing Gorr's campaign against the gods to the mobile-native Infinity Comic format.

subject: series
synopsis: Reprints of Jack Kirby's classic Tales of Asgard backup strips from the 1960s Journey into Mystery issues, presenting Norse mythology through Kirby's epic visual imagination and Stan Lee's bombastic prose. An essential artifact of the Marvel Silver Age and the foundation of Thor's mythological world-building.
author: Stan Lee

subject: series
synopsis: Walter Simonson's legendary run reinvented Thor with operatic grandeur, introducing Beta Ray Bill and the cataclysmic Surtur Saga with kinetic art that remains unmatched.
author: Walter Simonson

subject: series
synopsis: The annual anthology published for the Thought Bubble Comics Festival in Leeds, UK, featuring work from a rotating cast of British and international creators. A reliable showcase for current comics talent.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's collected edition of the ThunderCats licensed comic series based on the beloved 1980s animated franchise, following Lion-O, Cheetara, and the ThunderCats against Mumm-Ra.

subject: series
synopsis: Dan Jurgens's digital-first Titans series following the team as they face increasing threats, serving primarily as a companion to the main Titans book with accessible self-contained stories.
author: Dan Jurgens

subject: series
synopsis: Mia Goodwin's Action Lab series: teenage Addison Bramble becomes a vigilante killing those behind her loved ones' deaths while imagining herself a magical girl.
author: M. Goodwin

subject: series
synopsis: Gilbert Shelton's spin-off of The Fabulous Furry Freak Brothers: gag strips starring Fat Freddy's lazy, cunning cat.

subject: series
synopsis: A crossover event pitting Nick Fury's black-ops Avengers team against the official Ultimates, embroiled in a Zodiac conspiracy; notable primarily for its chaotic production history and the death of multiple Ultimate Universe characters.
author: Mark Millar

subject: series
synopsis: A crossover miniseries uniting the classic Japanese tokusatsu hero Ultraman with Marvel's Avengers in a kaiju-scale threat that brings both franchises together in a licensed collaboration.

subject: series
synopsis: Ablaze's adult horror-dark fantasy series featuring a demon and an angel whose cosmic conflict takes a very unexpected romantic turn, combining supernatural action with explicit adult content. One of Ablaze's more distinctive licensed European titles.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2006 five-issue Underworld mini: small-time enforcer Jackie Dio's transformation into a super-powered villain.

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Waid and Howard Porter's 1995 event: the demon Neron offers DC's villains power in exchange for their souls, then targets the heroes.
author: Mark Waid

subject: series
synopsis: Scott Snyder and Charles Soule's series set in a near-future where the United States has been sealed off from the world for thirty years; an international team ventures inside to uncover what happened and find a cure for a global plague.
author: Scott Snyder, Charles Soule

subject: series
synopsis: Acclaim's unfinished 1999 Unity 2000 mini, reuniting original Valiant heroes; cancelled before its conclusion.

subject: series
synopsis: Matt Kindt's 2013 Valiant Unity: Toyo Harada assembles Ninjak, Livewire, Eternal Warrior and Gilad to stop X-O Manowar, and the team stays together.

subject: series
synopsis: Pierre Christin and Jean-Claude Mézières's visionary Franco-Belgian sci-fi series following spatio-temporal agents Valérian and Laureline across time and space; hugely influential on science fiction visual design, inspiring Star Wars and countless films.
author: Pierre Christin

subject: series
synopsis: Christopher Priest and Ergün Gündüz's 2019 Vampirella: a dense, satirical reinvention of the Drakulon vampire heroine.

subject: series
synopsis: Dark romantic horror series revisiting the complicated and often violent relationship between Vampirella and Dracula, exploring their twisted bond and mutual destruction.
author: Tom Sniegoski

subject: series
synopsis: A tie-in to the Venom War event focusing on the Carnage symbiote's role in the conflict between Eddie Brock and Dylan Brock's competing claims to the Venom legacy.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A Venom War tie-in following the legacy of the Lethal Protector identity as multiple characters navigate their symbiote bonds amid the larger war between the Venoms.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A Venom War tie-in exploring the zombified symbiote hosts — the Zombiotes — as a faction, expanding the event's horror-inflected mythology.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's anthology series reprinting classic 1950s romance and suspense comics from Charlton, ACG, and Quality, offering charming period-earnest melodrama with the unintentional comedy of dated gender attitudes.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Bronze Age war anthology series featuring standalone stories about World War II and other conflicts, later repurposed into the horror anthology series with Death as narrator. A competent genre entry in Marvel's Bronze Age non-superhero line.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A companion series to Infinity Crusade following Adam Warlock's cosmic adventures and the ongoing struggle for the Infinity Gems, continuing the storylines from Infinity War and Gauntlet.
author: Jim Starlin

subject: series
synopsis: Dark Horse archival reprint volume of EC Comics' Weird Science, part of the ongoing EC Archives hardcover reprint program collecting the celebrated science fiction anthology that featured some of the finest sci-fi comics storytelling of the 1950s.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's long-running parody anthology series spoofing the publisher's own characters and comics with irreverent humor.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Matthew Rosenberg and Tyler Boss's post-apocalyptic coming-of-age story set in a world where roving gangs of teens survive by following strict genre rules — the music you listen to determines your tribe. Stylishly designed and emotionally earnest, it blends Mad Max energy with YA heart.
